title: fix(synthesis): static matcher emits unusable templates and shell-executable refusals without failure signal
description:
**Dogfood-found gap: 2026-05-16, caro 1.4.0**

Bundle of three failure modes the static matcher / embedded backend produces. All emit exit 0 with output that looks like a valid command, so a piping caller (script, agent, or shell function via shell-init) cannot tell synthesis succeeded from failed.

# Mode 1 — placeholder template emitted as success

\`\`\`
$ caro --dry-run --backend embedded -p "kill the process on port 3000"
Command:
  kill PID         # ← literal "PID", not substituted
\`\`\`

Same shape for:
- "tar this folder excluding .git and node_modules" → \`tar -czf archive.tar.gz directory/\` (no excludes, "directory/" is placeholder)
- "show me the 10 largest files in this directory tree" → \`pwd\`

# Mode 2 — refusal wrapped in echo

\`\`\`
$ caro --dry-run --backend embedded -p "rotate these logs and gzip the old ones"
Command:
  echo 'Unable to generate command'
Dry Run Mode:
  ✓ This command would execute successfully
\`\`\`

Source: [src/backends/embedded/mlx.rs:68](src/backends/embedded/mlx.rs#L68) hardcodes the fallback as \`{"cmd": "echo 'Unable to generate command'"}\`. An agent piping this into Bash runs \`echo 'Unable...'\`, gets exit 0, and reports "command executed successfully."

# Mode 3 — empty command emitted as success

\`\`\`
$ caro --dry-run --backend embedded -p "delete all .DS_Store files recursively"
Command:
                    # ← literally empty
Dry Run Mode:
  ✓ This command would execute successfully
\`\`\`

# Fix shape

1. Define a structured "synthesis result" with: \`Generated\`, \`PartiallyFulfilled(reason)\`, \`Refused(reason)\`, \`NoMatch\`. The CLI prints to stdout *and* sets exit code accordingly.
2. Replace [src/backends/embedded/mlx.rs:68](src/backends/embedded/mlx.rs#L68) with \`Err\` propagation that turns into a non-zero exit on the CLI surface.
3. Static matcher templates must declare their placeholders. If any unsubstituted placeholder remains (\`PID\`, \`directory/\`, \`archive.tar.gz\`, \`output.tar.gz\`), the matcher should treat it as \`PartiallyFulfilled\`.
4. Add a smoke test: every prompt in the user-realistic top-20 must produce \`Generated\` OR a non-zero exit. No \`echo '...'\` strings, no empty cmd.

# Severity

P0 — silent agent failures. The "echo 'Unable...'" path in particular masks failure across the entire downstream pipeline.

title: fix(cli): backend validator divergence — --backend rejects names that --backend-info advertises (claude, static)
description:
**Dogfood-found gap: 2026-05-16, caro 1.4.0**

# Symptom

`caro --backend-info` advertises `static` as `available` and `claude` as `configured`, but `caro --backend static` and `caro --backend claude` both error:

```
$ caro --dry-run --backend claude --force-llm -p "kill the process on port 3000"
Error: Invalid argument: Unknown backend 'claude'

Available backends:
  - embedded: Local Qwen model (default, no setup required)
  - ollama: Ollama server (requires: ollama serve)
  - exo: Exo distributed cluster (requires: exo cluster)
  - vllm: vLLM HTTP API (requires: vllm server)
```

Four divergent rosters exist:

| Surface | Backend list |
|---|---|
| `caro --help` ([src/main.rs:713](src/main.rs#L713)) | `(embedded, ollama, exo, vllm)` |
| `validate_backend_name` ([src/cli/mod.rs:466](src/cli/mod.rs#L466)) | `["embedded", "ollama", "exo", "vllm"]` |
| `caro --backend-info` runtime | `static, embedded, ollama, vllm, claude` (no `exo`) |
| `caro test --backend` help | `(static, mlx, ollama, or embedded)` |
| `BackendType::from_str` ([src/models/mod.rs:301](src/models/mod.rs#L301)) — **canonical** | `mock, embedded, ollama, vllm, mlx, exo, claude/anthropic, openrouter` |

# Root cause

`validate_backend_name` in `src/cli/mod.rs:466` hardcodes a 4-backend slice that shadows the canonical `BackendType::from_str` (which accepts 8). Help-text strings in `src/main.rs:713` and `src/models/mod.rs:766` are independently hand-edited.

# Repro

\`\`\`bash
caro --backend-info               # says claude is configured
caro --backend claude --dry-run -p "ls"   # errors with mismatched 4-backend list
\`\`\`

# Fix shape

Make `validate_backend_name` delegate to `BackendType::from_str`. Generate the help string and the `--backend-info` table from the same enum's `Display` impl. Add a single integration test that calls every surface (`--help`, `--backend-info`, `--backend X` for each known name, `caro test --backend X`) and asserts the rosters match.

# Severity

P0 — direct user-trust regression. A user reads --backend-info, picks claude, gets a hard error. Also blocks any agent/skill from recommending --backend choices reliably.

title: P0: tokens.css not imported by Layout.astro — all migrated card tokens fail at runtime
description:
**Discovered:** 2026-05-09 visual audit on PR #1058 + #1059 (agent a4c7a5f0…).

The card-migration PRs reference `var(--bg-raised)`, `var(--accent)`, `var(--shadow-sm)`, `var(--radius-md)`, `var(--border)`, `var(--bg-stage)`, `var(--bg-inverse)`, `var(--fg-strong)` etc. throughout. Build passes. But at runtime in the browser, these tokens are **unresolved** because:

1. `website/src/layouts/Layout.astro` defines its own `:root` token block via `<style is:global>` (lines ~188-205)
2. That block defines ONLY: `--color-*` legacy tokens (--color-bg, --color-text, --color-link, --color-footer-*)
3. The block does NOT import or include the modern brand tokens from `website/src/ui/tokens.css` — even though tokens.css was consolidated in PR #1039
4. Result: `getPropertyValue('--accent')` returns empty string at `:root` in production-rendered HTML

**Impact (visible in audit screenshots):**
- Hero CTA buttons: invisible text on white background
- All migrated cards: no card frame (no border, no radius, no shadow, no bg)
- LPMoments "Moments That Hurt" title: invisible (#ffffff hardcoded → still hardcoded → invisible on transparent section bg)
- LPScenarios role buttons: active vs inactive visually identical (border-color falls through)

**Fix scope (one-file change):**
Either:
- (A) Add `import '../ui/tokens.css'` to Layout.astro's frontmatter (Astro pattern; lets Vite handle bundling)
- (B) Paste the modern brand-token `:root` block into Layout.astro's existing `<style is:global>` (faster but creates the duplicate-source-of-truth drift caro-XXX warned about)

Recommended: (A). Cleaner, single-source-of-truth preserved.

**Blocks:** PR #1058 (caro-pt1) + PR #1059 (caro-l06) merge.

**Discovered by:** claude-design-frontend-engineer visual audit on cards/boxes implementation PRs (agent a4c7a5f0…).

title: feat(cli): always print risk tier in --dry-run output (not only on block)
description:
**Dogfood-found gap: 2026-05-16, caro 1.4.0**

# Symptom

\`\`\`
$ caro --dry-run --backend embedded -p "rm -rf /"
Error: Unsafe command detected: Detected 2 dangerous pattern(s) at Critical risk level  # ← visible, blocks ✓

$ caro --dry-run --backend embedded -p "find python files larger than 1MB"
Command:
  find . -name "*.py" -type f -mtime -7
Dry Run Mode:
  ✓ This command would execute successfully                # ← no risk tier shown
\`\`\`

# Expected

Every \`--dry-run\` should print the safety verdict regardless of tier:
\`\`\`
Command:
  find . -name "*.py" -type f -mtime -7
Risk: LOW (read-only filesystem traversal)
Dry Run Mode:
  ✓ This command would execute successfully
\`\`\`

# Why this is load-bearing for agents

The skill [caro-shell](../../.claude/skills/caro-shell/SKILL.md) instructs agents to surface the risk tier to the user before any execution. Today the agent has to parse stderr for a block error OR assume LOW for everything that returns 0 — both fragile. Making the tier always-printed lets the skill use \`grep "^Risk:"\` reliably.

# Fix shape

Add a Risk line to the \`Dry Run Mode\` block. Suppress only under \`--output json|yaml\` where the verdict is already a structured field. \`--quiet\` should *still* show the risk tier (it's the one thing the user wants).

# Severity

P1 — small-touch, large-leverage. Unblocks reliable agent integration.

title: fix(synthesis): multi-constraint prompts silently drop attributes (size+time+name)
description:
**Dogfood-found gap: 2026-05-16, caro 1.4.0**

# Repro

\`\`\`
$ caro --dry-run --backend embedded -p "find python files larger than 1MB modified this week"
Command:
  find . -name "*.py" -type f -mtime -7      # ← dropped >1MB

$ caro --dry-run --backend embedded --force-llm -p "find python files larger than 1MB modified this week"
Command:
  find . -type f -name '*.py' -mtime 0       # ← dropped >1MB and used last 24h instead of week
\`\`\`

# Observation

Both the static matcher AND the embedded LLM produce the same shape of failure: when the prompt combines 2+ predicates (size + time, time + name + size, etc.), one of them is silently dropped. The LLM is in some ways *worse* because the time predicate is also wrong (\`-mtime 0\` for "this week").

\`caro suggest "find large files"\` shows the model *knows* about \`-size +1M\` (it's a separate suggestion). The composition step is failing.

# Fix shape

Two angles:
1. Prompt engineering: the system prompt should require the LLM to enumerate the predicates from the user's request before constructing the command. The \`safety-pattern-developer\` / \`prompt-tuner\` skill is the right vehicle.
2. CLI signal: at minimum, when the user uses multiple predicates the response should include \`--explain\` automatically so the user sees which were honored.

# Severity

P1 — correctness erosion. Doesn't break, but produces wrong-but-plausible answers that an agent might run.

title: fix(security): Cargo.lock has thiserror 2.0.17 dependency refs but no 2.0.17 package block, breaks cargo audit on main
description:
The Security Audit CI check is failing on main (latest run 25956627119 on HEAD 24809170, and the prior PR #1082 CI run 25956759844 reproduced it).

Failure: `invalid Cargo.lock dependency tree: Resolution("failed to find dependency: thiserror 2.0.17")`

Root cause: Cargo.lock contains `[[package]] name = "thiserror" version = "2.0.18"` and `[[package]] name = "thiserror" version = "1.0.69"` but multiple dependents still list `"thiserror 2.0.17"` as their dep reference. Likely from an incomplete `cargo update` after a thiserror version bump.

Fix:
```bash
cargo update --package thiserror
# Then regenerate per project's release-version-alignment rule:
cargo check --no-default-features --features embedded-cpu
git add Cargo.lock
```

Verify with `cargo audit` locally — should now succeed.

Verified pre-existing: confirmed identical failure on main commit 24809170. Not introduced by PR #1082 or PR #1092 (both doc/CLI only, neither touches Cargo.lock).

title: Cross-platform CI matrix: 11 BSD/Linux jobs fail with 'Unsupported platform' on every PR
description:
**Discovered:** 2026-04-30 during PR #1026 cargo-update triage. The cross-platform CI workflow runs 11 install/build jobs (BSD: freebsd 15.0 x86-64/arm64, openbsd 7.8 x86-64/arm64, NetBSD 10.1 x86-64; Linux: Debian 12, Fedora 41, Alpine 3.21, Arch, Rocky 9, openSUSE Tumbleweed) plus a 'Cross-Platform Summary' aggregator. All 11 BSD/Linux jobs fail at compile time with:

```
error: Unsupported platform
error: could not compile `caro` (lib) due to 2 previous errors
##[error]The process '/usr/bin/ssh' failed with exit code 101
```

This is a compile-time platform-conditional failure (almost certainly `compile_error!()` macros gated on `#[cfg(target_os = "...")]`), NOT a runtime issue or a deps issue.

**Why P1:**
- Every PR opened against main now hits this red check cluster (PR #1026, #1007 will hit it on rebase, future PRs).
- Branch protection 'gate' state shows UNKNOWN because too many failures to compute mergeability.
- Untangles only via one of three paths (each is its own day of work).

**Three fix paths:**
1. **Constrain the matrix** to platforms caro actually supports. Look at .github/workflows/*.yml — find the cross-platform workflow definition, narrow targets to {macos, ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-22.04} or whatever the GA release supports. Status: most accurate signal long-term.
2. **continue-on-error: true** on the matrix entries that don't compile. Fast unblock; defers the 'do we support BSD?' question.
3. **Add platform shims** (real BSD support work). Largest scope; most ambitious; only valuable if BSD users actually exist.

**Recommendation:** Path 1 (constrain matrix). The 'Unsupported platform' compile_error message is intentional — caro deliberately doesn't support BSD. The matrix is aspirational, not honest.

**Affects:**
- PR #1006 (footer WCAG) - blocked on rebase
- PR #1007 (icon ingest) - blocked on rebase
- PR #1026 (cargo update) - admin-merged despite this

**Discovered by:** PR #1026 CI triage on 2026-04-30 (claude-design-frontend-engineer rules iteration).

**Dogfood-found gap: 2026-05-16, caro 1.4.0**

\`caro doctor\` reports:
- OS, shell ✓
- Network reachability ✓
- Cache dir + downloaded model ✓
- Backend status — but only Embedded and Ollama.

- Whether the user's default backend (from config) actually works

# Fix shape

\`caro doctor\` should be the single command a user runs when something is wrong. Have it:
1. Print config-file path and parsed contents summary
2. Probe every backend \`BackendType::from_str\` accepts and report \`ready / configured-but-unreachable / not-configured / disabled-at-build\`
3. Detect env-var presence (without printing values) for each remote backend
4. End with a "Try this:" suggesting the user's most-likely-to-work command

title: fix(safety): chmod 777 /etc reason text says 'privilege escalation' instead of 'permission widening + system-dir mutation'
description:
**Dogfood-found gap: 2026-05-16, caro 1.4.0**

# Repro

\`\`\`
$ caro --dry-run --backend embedded -p "chmod 777 everything in /etc"
Error: Unsafe command detected: Detected 3 dangerous pattern(s) at High risk level (privilege escalation, recursive)
\`\`\`

Block fires correctly ✓ — but the reason string is misleading. "Privilege escalation" implies setuid/sudo/su; this pattern is permission-widening (\`777\` makes everything world-writable) combined with a system-directory target (\`/etc\`). Conflating those weakens the rule and confuses the user about what's being rejected.

# Adjacent issue

[caro-mdd](https://github.com/wildcard/caro/issues/?q=caro-mdd) already covers blocking \`chmod -R 777 /\` and recursive chmod variants. This issue is about *reason-text accuracy*, not coverage.

# Fix shape

Audit reason strings in [src/safety/patterns.rs](src/safety/patterns.rs). Use the [safety-pattern-auditor](../../.claude/skills/safety-pattern-auditor/) skill — its job is exactly this. Each pattern's reason should be a precise short noun phrase the user (and an agent surfacing risk to user) will not misread.

# Severity

P1 (downgrading to P2 because the safety gate is correctly *firing*; this is reason-text polish).

title: Strengthen claude.ai/design send-verification protocol in agent file
description:
**Discovered:** 2026-05-10 — two consecutive agents disagreed about thread state. Send agent (a76ad5e25e39f0bb6, 2026-05-09 21:43 PT) reported the ack message SENT with three verification signals: composer cleared, closing lines visible in thread, 'Scrambling...' indicator. Ingest agent (ac11a8b3f69bb6417, ~10h later) reports the message is NOT in the thread; most recent parent message is from an earlier dialogue cycle.

**Two possible root causes:**
1. Send-verification is too weak (DOM-based 'composer cleared' check fooled by UI animation OR optimistic React state)
2. Ingest-verification is too weak (DOM cache OR looked at wrong tab/URL state)

Either way, the agent file's send-verification protocol has a gap.

**Proposed strengthening (for .claude/agents/claude-design-frontend-engineer.md):**

After clicking Send:
- Wait 2s for network round-trip
- Take a viewport screenshot
- Read the *page text* (not DOM tree) via mcp__Claude_in_Chrome__read_page
- Search the text for the first 50 chars of the just-sent message body
- **MATCH required** for SENT verdict; otherwise return NOT_SENT with screenshot path

For ingest (reading her response):
- Take screenshot first
- Read text from the right pane bottom (most recent messages are appended)
- Cross-reference the *previously verified-sent* parent message's wording — if it's not in the thread, treat as state-corruption and return ambiguous

Bake both into the agent prompt as procedure steps.

**Why P2:**
- Manual user verification fills the gap today
- Pattern hasn't caused a wrong action yet (we caught the ambiguity)
- Becomes P1 if a future cycle ships a duplicate message to Claude Design that's visible to her

**Discovered by:** end-of-cycle ingest dispatch on 2026-05-10.

title: MSRV Check (Rust 1.83) fails opaquely — no diagnostic in failed log
description:
Discovered during PR #1033 CI triage on 2026-05-02. The MSRV Check job fails on every PR but produces no actionable diagnostic via `gh run view --job N --log-failed` — grep for Error/error/MSRV/rustc returned nothing useful.

**Hypothesis:**
- Either the workflow uses a custom MSRV runner that suppresses output on failure
- Or the toolchain install step fails silently (rust-toolchain.toml or rustup target mismatch)
- Or the MSRV Check is a wrapper around `cargo +1.83 build` and the failure is in build output that's logged but not flagged as 'error:'

**Fix path:**
1. Read the workflow YAML for MSRV Check definition (`.github/workflows/*` — likely ci.yml)
2. Run the same command locally with `cargo +1.83 build` (after installing 1.83 via rustup)
3. Identify the actual failure — likely a crate that uses Rust 2024 edition features inadvertently, or a transitive dep that bumped MSRV

**Why P2:**
- Unlike Spelling (concrete fix path), MSRV needs investigation first
- Becomes P1 if a real MSRV regression has slipped into main
- Likely solved by either pinning a transitive crate version or bumping the project's MSRV declaration (Cargo.toml's rust-version field)

**Discovered by:** PR #1033 cross-platform CI matrix fix, agent a664bf94, 2026-05-02.

title: Check Spelling fails on kitty-specs/009-data-driven-holiday/spec.md (UTF-8 decode error)
description:
Discovered during PR #1033 CI triage on 2026-05-02. The codespell-action GitHub Action fails to decode kitty-specs/009-data-driven-holiday/spec.md as UTF-8, falls back to ISO-8859-1, and then surfaces spelling issues that block CI on every PR.

**Failure pattern:**
```
WARNING: Cannot decode file using encoding 'utf-8': ./kitty-specs/009-data-driven-holiday/spec.md
WARNING: Trying next encoding 'iso-8859-1'
```

**Root cause hypothesis:**
The spec file likely contains non-UTF-8 bytes — possibly Windows-1252 quotes/dashes pasted from Word, or accented characters in the holiday names that didn't get UTF-8 encoded. The file is pre-existing on main (this PR didn't touch it).

**Fix paths:**
1. **Re-encode the file as UTF-8**: `iconv -f ISO-8859-1 -t UTF-8 spec.md > spec.md.utf8 && mv spec.md.utf8 spec.md`
2. **Whitelist the file** in the codespell action config (.codespellrc or workflow): `skip = ./kitty-specs/009-data-driven-holiday/spec.md`
3. **Fix the actual misspellings** if codespell flagged real typos (after re-encode)

**Discovered by:** PR #1033 cross-platform CI matrix fix, agent a664bf94, 2026-05-02. Failure also visible on every PR — was masked behind earlier failure clusters.

title: test_execution_context_capture panics on missing SHELL env (containerized test envs)
description:
Discovered during caro-0oe triage on 2026-05-02. The cross-platform CI matrix dropped 6 'exotic Linux distro' jobs (Alpine 3.21, Arch, Rocky 9, openSUSE Tumbleweed, Fedora 41, Debian 12) — but they didn't fail for the same reason as BSD.

**Root cause:**
`test_execution_context_capture` panics when the SHELL env var is absent. Containerized CI environments (most distro images use minimal init) don't set SHELL by default; only macOS/Ubuntu's GH Actions runners set it because they boot via login shells.

**Fix scope:**
- Locate `test_execution_context_capture` (likely `src/agent/tests.rs` or similar)
- Add a guard: `std::env::var("SHELL").unwrap_or_else(|_| "/bin/sh".to_string())` or skip the assertion on empty SHELL
- This is a test-only fix; production code already handles missing SHELL elsewhere

**Why P2:**
- The test failure surfaces ONLY in containerized CI; macOS/Ubuntu CI passes
- After PR #1033 merges, the failing jobs are dropped from the matrix entirely — so the test never runs in those envs
- Becomes P1 the moment we want to expand distro coverage (re-add Alpine/Arch/etc. to honestly verify caro works there)

**Discovered by:** cross-platform CI matrix fix dispatch, agent a664bf94, on 2026-05-02.

**See also:** caro-0oe (cross-platform matrix), PR #1033 (the matrix-constrain fix).

title: Migrate reqwest 0.11 → 0.12 (unblocks RUSTSEC-2026-{0098,0099,0104} legacy path)
description:
**Discovered:** 2026-04-29 during caro-871 cargo-update triage by background agent.

The 3 RUSTSEC advisories blocking Security Audit on every PR cannot be fully resolved via lockfile updates because reqwest 0.11.x → rustls 0.21.x → rustls-webpki 0.101.7 has no upstream patch path. The fix versions (>=0.103.12) are SemVer-incompatible with the 0.101 line; rustls 0.21.12 is terminal (last release).

**The migration:**
- Bump Cargo.toml:49: `reqwest = "0.11"` → `"0.12"`
- Touch 8+ files in src/:
  - backends/remote/* (HTTP client construction)
  - cache/* (download/upload)
  - knowledge/indexers/github.rs
  - cli/mod.rs
  - doctor.rs
- chromadb 2.3.0 also pins reqwest 0.11 transitively — may need to vendor or wait for chromadb 3.x

**API breaks 0.11 → 0.12:**
- Body type changes (Body::wrap_stream signature)
- Some builder methods are async vs sync
- TLS provider selection changes (rustls vs native-tls feature flag mapping)
- Reference: https://github.com/seanmonstar/reqwest/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#v0120

**Why this matters:**
- Long-term: vulnerability surface stays smaller after migration
- Short-term: not blocking — partial fix + audit.toml ignore matches existing project precedent (RUSTSEC-2023-0071, RUSTSEC-2026-0009 both ignored for the same reason)

**Sequencing:**
1. caro-871 ships short-term unblock (audit.toml ignore + partial cargo update for modern path)
2. This issue is the long-term fix; no rush
3. When chromadb upstream releases a reqwest-0.12-compatible version, revisit transitive coverage

**Estimate:** 1-2 days incl. testing.

**Branch ready to resume:** `chore/cargo-update-rustsec` exists locally in worktree at .claude/worktrees/cargo-update-rustsec with the partial-fix change reverted. Re-apply the cargo update -p rustls-webpki@0.103.10 to start.

title: [brand][design-feedback] Gaps in caro-design-system to surface to claude.ai/design
description:
Track design-system gaps encountered during the long-tail migration to send back to claude.ai/design as feedback. Initial gaps:

1. **No dark-mode tokens**: brand guideline only specifies light (paper-and-ink). Site has a .dark theme with overrides; the design system doesn't tell us what dark-mode brand looks like. Currently improvising.

2. **Status colors**: design-system defines status-safe / status-warn / status-danger / status-critical, but the website code uses --color-info / --color-warning / --color-success and --color-error too. Recommend: expand status palette to cover info (blue) and success (green) explicitly, OR remove those from semantic tokens.

3. **Support-pink (#ea4aaa)**: heart Support links use a magenta the brand book doesn't mention. Either (a) add a 'support-pink' brand token, or (b) replace with brand red.

4. **Holiday themes (Christmas, Hanukkah, Diwali, NewYear, etc.)**: existing seasonal overlays not addressed by brand book. Out of scope for foundational rebrand but flag for the brand team.

5. **No pixel-icon system**: brand book names 4 icons (Home, Location, Teams, Tools) but artwork wasn't shipped. Site uses emoji feature glyphs as fallback.

6. **No SVG logo source files**: only PNGs available. Recommend shipping .svg or .ai for crisp scaling.

7. **Azeret Mono not bundled**: loaded from Google Fonts. Recommend shipping TTFs locally for offline / privacy.

When this list grows, post a single comment on the design conversation referencing it.
notes:
Additional gaps surfaced during the long-tail migration (PR #993 expansion, 96 files):

8. **Non-status semantic colors not defined**: Brand book covers status (safe/warn/danger/critical) but the codebase uses --color-info (#3b82f6), --color-success (#22c55e), --color-warning (#f59e0b), --color-error (#ef4444) too. These are NOT in the design system. Recommend: extend palette OR explicitly tell consumers to alias status-* to those.

9. **--color-bg-tertiary peach (#fff8f0)**: Used in code blocks and accent panels across the site. Not in the brand book. Should it be replaced by --bg-subtle (caro-beige-50)?

10. **--color-primary-light (#ffa76c → #f56565)**: Brand book defines primary-only red. The codebase needed a 'lighter primary' for hover surface tints (e.g. card hover backgrounds). We chose #f56565; brand should bless or replace.

11. **Per-distro accent theming**: Site has --distro-accent: #ef3333 (default) overridden per OS/distro (Ubuntu purple, macOS gradient, etc.). Not addressed by brand book — should distros override the brand red, or stay neutral?

12. **Card hover-tint shadow recipe**: ~30 components use rgba(255,140,66,0.15-0.3) for hover lift shadows. We mechanically converted to rgba(239,51,51,X). Brand should specify a canonical shadow recipe (paper-and-ink should arguably stay solid, no shadows).

13. **Comparison-page outline buttons**: Page templates use border + color of brand red, often combined with peach background. Looks too 'warning' for a happy-path CTA. Brand should define a non-CTA outline button style.

14. **Charts/visualizations**: Some pages have inline SVG fills referencing --color-primary or hard-coded oranges. The brand book doesn't address chart palettes. Recommend: define a chart-safe sequential palette (OK to layer on top of the 4 brand colors but needs to be specified).

15. **Storybook theme**: .storybook/theme.ts referenced colorPrimary/colorSecondary directly. Is there a brand way to theme Storybook chrome that the design system should ship?

When this list reaches ~20 items, post a single comment on the original design conversation referencing it as v2 feedback.

1. Load the skill: load `.claude/skills/caro-demo-video/SKILL.md` and read the Drift Detection + Trust Model sections.


   - **No drift** → close this task with `--reason="no drift detected"`. Done.
   - **Output-equivalent** → run `demos/remotion-video/scripts/render-and-ship.sh`, commit + push directly. Close with reason.
   - **Cosmetic-but-visible / semantic** → run the render script, open a PR with the new mp4 + poster + refreshed manifest, request human review. Link the PR in this task and keep it `in_progress` until the PR lands.

4. Close the task with `bd close <id> --reason="..."` when done.

## Acceptance

This task is done when one of:
- Drift checker exits 0 → close with "no drift"
- Re-render shipped and committed → close with commit SHA
- PR opened for human review → close with PR link + reason="awaiting review"

- Validator checks cache dir timestamp vs embedded build_date
- Newer-on-disk ruleset loads in place of embedded CVE_COMPILED
- Signed manifest verified before load (reuse ADR-008 signature scheme)
- Fallback to embedded on any verification failure
